name: text
title: Text
description: Body and supporting text at a named role from the type scale.

base.summary: One type role and one foreground step. No box: text has no padding, no background and no margin of its own.

tokens.font-size: the chosen role's size — type.body.size, type.large.size, type.supporting.size or type.label.size
tokens.margin: space.0 — the page owns the space between blocks, for the reason Heading's contract gives

label.summary: The label role carries two things the others do not, and they come from the scale rather than from here.

tokens.letter-spacing: type.label.letter-spacing — uppercase text needs the extra tracking to stay readable, which is why that step exists

tone.summary: The three documented foreground steps for text, and the reason this prop exists at all: it is the shortest path to the right colour, so nobody reaches for a palette token.

tokens.all three: contrast-verified against theme.bg.canvas, theme.bg.surface and theme.bg.subtle — see the contrast page

behavior.summary:
A `

` or a `` set to one named role of the type scale. No primitive and no state.

decisions.why: A heading enters the document outline and is a navigation target; body text is neither. That is a difference in semantics rather than in looks, which is this system's test for splitting a component — the same test that separated Tabs from SegmentedControl. A single `as="h2"` prop here could not require a level only when the element happens to be a heading, and a heading without a level is the bug both components exist to prevent.

Those are the two things running text is: a block of prose, or a run inside one. `div` is the one that would turn this into a layout wrapper — and a `<div>` holding text is how a component like this stops being about type and starts being about boxes. A text block that must contain block content is not one paragraph and should not pretend to be.

decisions.decision: `tone` is part of it, even though the type roles carry no colour
decisions.why: The type scale is size, weight and line-height only, so a caller styling text still has to pick a foreground — and picking wrongly is this system's most common token error, which `internal/vibe-tests` exists to measure. Three named steps that map onto the three documented and contrast-verified `theme.fg.*` values make the correct choice the shortest one. It is deliberately not open-ended: a role colour or a status colour on running text is a different decision, and Notice owns it.

`type.code` exists, but inline code is a `<code>` ELEMENT — a semantic claim about the content, not a size. Offering it as a role would mean either rendering the wrong element or accepting `as="code" role="code"`, which says the same thing twice. Inline code belongs to a base layer styling `code` directly, which `@rata/css` does not ship yet and which is a separate gap from this component.

decisions.decision: No line clamping in this version
decisions.why: `-webkit-line-clamp` is the only way to truncate at a line count and it needs three coupled declarations plus a fixed display mode, which changes how the element lays out — and truncated text needs its full value reachable some other way or the content is simply gone. It deserves its own pass rather than riding along with the scale.

use: A paragraph, a sentence of help text, an eyebrow label.
dont: Block content inside `as="p"`. A paragraph cannot contain a list or another paragraph, and the browser will silently close it early.
children.a11y: Plain content. Nothing here is announced as anything but text, which is the point.

as.summary: Whether this is a block of text or a run inside one.
use: `span` for text inside a sentence, a row or a control's label area.
dont: `span` for a paragraph. It is not a block, so the page's spacing rules will not apply to it.
as.a11y: Neither element carries a role, so this changes nothing that is announced — it changes what the text is, structurally, for spacing and for selection.

role.summary: Which step of the scale this text is set at.
use: `supporting` for help text under a field, a timestamp, secondary metadata in a row.
`large` for a standfirst — one paragraph introducing a page, set above body size.
`label` for an uppercase eyebrow over a section or a group of fields.
dont: `supporting` to mean disabled. It is smaller, not dimmer, and it is still meant to be read — `tone` is the prop that changes emphasis.
role.a11y: `label` renders uppercase through `text-transform`, so the text stays lowercase in the accessibility tree and a screen reader does not spell it out letter by letter. Typing it in capitals would.

tone.summary: Which of the three documented foreground steps it takes.
use: `secondary` for text that supports the primary content and is still read in full.
`muted` for the least prominent text on a surface — a placeholder-like hint, a disabled row's caption.
dont: A status or accent colour. Those belong to a role, and running text carrying one reads as a link or an error; Notice is the component for a coloured message.
`muted` for anything load-bearing. It is the lowest of the three and the first to fail on an unusual background.
tone.a11y: All three are contrast-verified against canvas, surface and subtle. None of them is below the text floor — this prop cannot make text fail contrast on a documented background, which is why it is a closed set of three rather than a colour.

className.summary: Extra classes, for placement — not for restyling it.
use: The margin or measure the page wants, neither of which this component owns.
dont: Overriding size or colour. Those are `role` and `tone`, and a hand-written value drifts from the scale the moment the seed moves.
